figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 1.   Functions of fMccA peptide. (A) Left, biosynthesis of McC from fMccA in producing cells. Right, proteolysis of McC to 2, an inert analogue of aspRS 
intermediate 3, inside sensitive cells. The N-­terminal formyl group and C-­terminal Asn/Asp residues are shown in red and blue, respectively. The phosphoramidate 
and corresponding phosphoester bonds are highlighted by pink ellipse. (B) Structure of fMccAGGK-­FITC. Linker residues (GlyGlyLys) and FITC are shown in orange 
and green, respectively. (C) FP curve for fMccAGGK-­FITC recognition by YejA. Competition FP curves for fMccAGGK-­FITC recognition by YejA using fMccA (D), MccA 
(E), and McC (F) as competitors, respectively. Error bars represent the SD of the mean (n = 3).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 2.   Overall structural analysis of YejA in complex with McC. (A) Complex of YejA and McC with the two domains represented as green and cyan ribbons. (B) 
Superimposition of structures of McC-­bound YejA (green) and the apo MbnE (light gray). (C) The difference Fourier map (FO – FC) contoured at 2.0 σ (gray) is shown 
for electron density revealing the occupancy for McC peptide region (orange sticks). (D) Surface cutaway of the complex structure of YejA and McC (purple for 
peptide and orange for 3-­aminopropyl adenylate moiety). The maximum width of the cavity is shown by a blue dashed line.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 3.   Ligand binding sites in YejA. (A) Close-­up view of ligand binding sites in structure of YejA bound to fMccA (purple sticks). The difference Fourier map 
(gray) is contoured at level of 2.0 σ revealing the occupancy for the entire fMccA. Critical YejA residues are represented as green and cyan sticks. Interactions 
between fMccA (formyl group and Arg2) and YejA residues are indicated by blue dash lines and distances (Å). (B) The results of FP binding assays for wild-­type 
and variants of YejA. The functions of individual residues are indicated. (C) Close-­up view of formyl group binding sites in structure of S481A YejA variant bound 
to McC (yellow sticks). The difference Fourier map (gray) is contoured at level of 2.0 σ revealing the occupancy for the peptide region. (D) Interactions between 
fMccA (Asn5 and Asn7) and YejA residues are indicated by blue dash lines and distances (Å).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 4.   Transport of FITC into E. coli facilitated by fMccA. Confocal microscopic images of E. coli cells after incubation with the mixture of fMccAGGK and FITC 
(A, bright field; B, fluorescence; C, overlay) and with fMccAGGK-­FITC (D, bright field; E, fluorescence; F, overlay).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 5.   fMccA remodels the activity spectrum of antibiotics. (A) Structures of eperezolid, NH2-­eperezolid, gly-­ciprofloxacin, and conjugates 4-­6. (B) Antibacterial 
activities (MIC in μM) against nine strains. * indicates that the genomes of these strains are not available and assumptively encode YejA homologs. NA indicates 
that the MICs were not determined. The sequence identity and coverage with YejA are indicated in the parentheses. (C) Quantification curves of 4-­6 after 
incubation in human serum.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 6.   Distribution and conservation of YejA-­like transporters. (A) SSN of 263 
nonredundant YejA-­like transporters, separated by 60% sequence identity. 
Nodes are colored by their corresponding family, and cluster numbers are 
assigned. The node representing YejA is highlighted by a white circle. WebLogo 
frequency plots for the fMccA/McC-­binding residues of YejA-­like transporters 
from SSN clusters (B) 1, (C) 2, and (D) 3. The positions of fMccA/McC-­binding 
residues identified in YejA are indicated above the WebLogo using the residue 
number of YejA. Residues are colored according to their hydrophobicity.
